Time from an infection to the first relapse of its hypnozoite batch

Source: R/metrics.R
time_to_relapse.Rd

One row per hypnozoite batch: the hypnozoites one genotype of a bite or an import laid down in a host, so a bite that delivers two genotypes can lay down two. A batch's clock starts on the day it was established, the day of the bite, or for an import that also brought a blood-stage infection, the day after it. Founder hosts carry no batch until a bite or an import gives them one.

Usage

time_to_relapse(run, emptied = c("censor", "follow"), exclude_masked = FALSE)

Arguments

run

a run: a vivax_run (from run_sim() or load_run()) or the path of a run directory.

emptied

"censor" (stop the clock on the day a batch empties without relapsing) or "follow" (follow it to SIM_DAYS).

exclude_masked

if TRUE, the first relapse is the first that is not masked.

Value

a data.table, one row per batch, by batch_tick and batch_pedigree_id: batch_pedigree_id, human_id, lineage_id, imported (an imported batch), batch_tick (the day it was established), n_hypnozoites (its size then), time (days from batch_tick to the first relapse or to censoring), event (1 relapse, 0 censored) and end_reason ("relapse", "emptied" or "run_end"). A run with no batch gives no row.

Details

The clock stops at the batch's first relapse (event = 1). Without one (event = 0) it stops on the day the batch's last hypnozoite left it, by death or radical cure (emptied = "censor"), or at the run's last day, SIM_DAYS, for a batch that still held hypnozoites then, and with emptied = "follow" for one that emptied without relapsing too. Censoring at emptying gives the time to relapse of the hypnozoites that live; following to the end gives the curve a trial reports, where radical cure shows as relapses prevented.

With exclude_masked = TRUE a masked relapse, into a patent clone of its own lineage (see classify_cases()), does not stop the clock, although its hypnozoites leave the batch: the first relapse is the first a study could see as a recurrence.

See also

plot_relapse_km(), dormancy_durations()

Examples

tt <- time_to_relapse(example_run())
head(tt)
#>    batch_pedigree_id human_id lineage_id imported batch_tick n_hypnozoites
#>                <int>    <int>     <char>   <lgcl>      <int>         <int>
#> 1:                52       10          7    FALSE         13             5
#> 2:                99       40          4    FALSE         28             7
#> 3:               128       10        127     TRUE         34             1
#> 4:               154       50          8    FALSE         43             1
#> 5:               173       14        172     TRUE         54             1
#> 6:               185       27        184     TRUE         63             5
#>     time event end_reason
#>    <int> <int>     <char>
#> 1:    20     1    relapse
#> 2:    22     1    relapse
#> 3:   128     0    emptied
#> 4:     4     0    emptied
#> 5:    84     1    relapse
#> 6:    20     1    relapse
